narrativeReportMd:
# FamilyMemberHistory R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`FamilyMemberHistory` keeps the same canonical resource identity, but R6 introduces several local breaking and round-trip changes. The highest-impact R4-to-R6 breaks are removal of `instantiatesCanonical`/`instantiatesUri`, removal of `estimatedAge`, replacement of `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` by `reason: CodeableReference`, and a new error invariant forbidding `age[x]` together with `deceased[x]`.

## Scope
The analysis covers the base resource StructureDefinition and local FamilyMemberHistory elements, constraints, bindings, flags, and semantic text. Inherited `DomainResource`, `Element`, `BackboneElement`, and datatype changes are not reported as local findings.

## Main migration themes
R4-to-R6 migration needs structural transforms for removed or merged fields and policy decisions for data that R6 no longer has a native slot for, especially `estimatedAge` and protocol-instantiation metadata. R6-to-R4 conversion also becomes lossy for new R6 content such as `procedure`, `recorder`, `asserter`, and `CodeableReference`-based `reason`.

## Highest-impact findings
The strongest validation break is the new `fhs-3` invariant: an R4 instance that records both the relative's age and death information can become invalid. The `reason` conversion is also high impact because it changes element names and introduces the R6-only `CodeableReference` pattern.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for records with deceased relatives, approximate ages, family-history procedures, and allergy/intolerance semantics because automated conversion can otherwise lose clinical nuance.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could have been less disruptive if old optional elements had been retained as deprecated aliases or if stricter semantics had been introduced as warnings/profiles first. The `reason` change is probably aligned with a broader R6 `CodeableReference` pattern, but it is still a hard wire-format and codegen change.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate analyses should cover the `CodeableReference` datatype, base-resource inherited constraints, search parameters, related profiles/extensions, and terminology expansions.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 preserves the `FamilyMemberHistory` resource identity but makes local wire-format and validation changes. Top concerns are removed/merged elements (`instantiates*`, `estimatedAge`, `reasonCode`/`reasonReference`), the new `age[x]` versus `deceased[x]` invariant, and lossy R6-to-R4 handling for procedures and `CodeableReference` reasons. The main uncertainty is terminology detail for example/extensible bindings without full expansions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a real transform rather than a version-label update. Existing R4 data must be scanned for removed elements and for `age[x]` plus `deceased[x]`. R6 data exported back to R4 needs explicit loss-handling rules for new provenance-like actors, procedures, and `CodeableReference.reason` items. Generated models, serializers, FHIRPath expressions, and summary projections should be updated for renamed/removed properties and changed summary flags.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, constraint, flag, and binding-strength comparisons because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is medium for terminology and design-justification judgments because no official diff, Jira rationale, narrative pages, or terminology-server expansions were available.

findings.title: Protocol instantiation elements were removed

oldState.summary: R4 allowed `instantiatesCanonical` and `instantiatesUri`, both 0..* summary elements.

semanticText.definition: The elements linked the FamilyMemberHistory to a FHIR-defined or externally maintained protocol, guideline, order set, or other definition.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances could state that the family history adhered to one or more protocols or definitions using either a canonical URL or a general URI.

newState.summary: R6 has no local `instantiatesCanonical` or `instantiatesUri` element on FamilyMemberHistory.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 resource has no direct replacement element for this metadata.

facts.note: Both removed elements were summary elements in R4.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 differential and snapshot contain no same-named FamilyMemberHistory elements and no obvious renamed local protocol-instantiation counterpart.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format validation break: an R4 instance containing either removed property has an element that is not allowed by the R6 base resource. Generated R6 classes and strict parsers will also not expose those properties.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The data is protocol/provenance-like metadata rather than the family clinical facts themselves, but it can matter for auditability and guideline adherence.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify the resource or remove protocol-instantiation metadata from FamilyMemberHistory.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the optional R4 protocol-instantiation elements in base R6, marked deprecated or legacy, while directing new use to the preferred provenance or workflow mechanism.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Removing optional `instantiatesCanonical` and `instantiatesUri` creates a hard R4-to-R6 validation break without evidence in the local definitions that the protocol metadata was unsafe or impossible to keep. The likely cleanup goal is reasonable, but the same transition could have been staged in the base resource by retaining the elements as deprecated legacy content.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design is to keep both optional elements in R6, clarify their legacy status, and recommend a preferred R6 mechanism for new protocol/provenance metadata. A cross-version extension or conversion rule would only mitigate migration; it would not preserve R4-valid base instances. The tradeoff of the base-retention alternative is a larger resource surface and the risk that deprecated protocol fields never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances with only resource-surface clutter, but leaves legacy metadata fields that may persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `instantiatesCanonical` as 0..* canonical with target profiles for plan/questionnaire/activity/measure/operation definitions.
R4 defines `instantiatesUri` as 0..* uri.
No R6 FamilyMemberHistory element with either id is present.

examples.examplesMd: The example is a minimal R4-style instance fragment showing the removed properties; those property names have no R6 base-resource slot.

findings.narrativeMd: `FamilyMemberHistory.instantiatesCanonical` and `FamilyMemberHistory.instantiatesUri` disappear in R6. Existing R4 records that use these fields to say which protocol or definition a family-history collection followed will fail strict R6 validation unless the data is removed or carried by an extension or external resource.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance containing either removed element becomes R6-invalid because unknown elements are not allowed in the base resource. This affects JSON/XML parsers, generated models, FHIRPath expressions, and summary projections that referenced the old fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan R4 data for both fields. If the metadata is clinically or operationally important, preserve it in an agreed extension, Provenance/QuestionnaireResponse linkage, or implementation-specific mapping rather than silently dropping it. Regression tests should include instances with each removed field.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the old fields were optional, retaining them as deprecated elements would have been backward compatible. Removing them gives a cleaner R6 model but forces migration policy for historical protocol-adherence metadata.

findings.title: `estimatedAge` was removed

oldState.summary: R4 had optional `estimatedAge` 0..1 boolean, summary=true, conditioned by fhs-2.

constraints.human: Can only have estimatedAge if age[x] is present

semanticText.definition: If true, indicates that the age value specified is an estimated value.
semanticText.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the fact that age is estimated can/should change the results of any algorithm that calculates based on the specified age.
semanticText.meaningWhenMissing: It is unknown whether the age is an estimate or not

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed an explicit boolean qualifier to say that the relative's recorded age was estimated.

newState.summary: R6 has no `estimatedAge` element and the `age[x]` comment no longer points to it.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can still carry approximate-looking age values as `Age`, `Range`, or `string`, but it has no native boolean estimate flag on the resource.

facts.note: The constraint disappeared because the element it constrained was removed.

facts.oldValue: use estimatedAge to indicate whether the age is actual or not.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: No R6 same-named element or local replacement was found; a local package search found no R6 `estimatedAge` occurrence.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `estimatedAge` become R6-invalid. The harder migration problem is semantic loss: an approximate age indicator can affect risk calculations and cannot be copied into a native R6 boolean field.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Age precision is relevant to family-history risk interpretation, especially when age of onset or relative age feeds clinical decision support.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove a special-purpose approximation flag and rely on richer age representations such as ranges or strings.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional `estimatedAge` in base R6 as deprecated legacy content while preferring `Range`, approximate `Age`, or text where suitable.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R4 element was optional but carried clinically relevant precision information; its removal makes old instances invalid and can lose whether an age was explicitly estimated. The local StructureDefinitions show no reason that the R6 model needed to reject the old boolean rather than deprecate it.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would retain `estimatedAge` with legacy/deprecated guidance and keep any updated age-representation recommendations for new content. This is more than migration tooling because the old wire element would remain valid in base R6. The tradeoff is continued ambiguity between a separate estimate flag and approximate values represented as `Range` or string.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids validation failure and semantic loss, but preserves a resource-specific qualifier alongside other approximate-age representations.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `estimatedAge` as 0..1 boolean with summary=true and meaningWhenMissing text.
evidence.quote: If true, indicates that the age value specified is an estimated value.

evidence.detail: R4 invariant fhs-2 tied `estimatedAge` to presence of `age[x]`.
R6 has no `FamilyMemberHistory.estimatedAge` element.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example preserves the human-readable approximation but loses the explicit boolean estimate flag unless an extension is added.

findings.narrativeMd: `estimatedAge` was a local R4 element for a clinically meaningful qualifier: the stated age is estimated. R6 removes it without an obvious local replacement, so old data either fails validation or must be converted into less precise text/range/extension semantics.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Any R4 instance that includes `estimatedAge` is old-valid/new-invalid. Removing the field can also break code generated from R4 models and FHIRPath logic that used the boolean flag. R6-to-R4 representability is not the issue; the risk is R4-to-R6 semantic loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Identify all records with `estimatedAge`. If `age[x]` is already a string such as "about 70", retaining the string may be adequate for display but not for algorithms. For computable preservation, define a cross-version extension or map to a `Range` only when the source semantics support that conversion. Review decision-support tests that depend on age precision.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal was avoidable from a wire-format compatibility perspective because the element was optional. A deprecated element or standard extension would have allowed old data to remain valid while nudging new implementations toward preferred age representations.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Manual review is advisable before dropping the flag because it can alter risk algorithms that distinguish exact from estimated ages.

findings.title: New invariant forbids `age[x]` together with `deceased[x]`

oldState.summary: R4 had fhs-1 forbidding `age[x]` with `born[x]`, but no invariant forbidding `age[x]` with `deceased[x]`.

constraints.human: Can have age[x] or born[x], but not both

oldState.narrativeMd: An R4 instance could carry the relative's age and also carry death status, date, or age-at-death information.

newState.summary: R6 adds error invariant fhs-3: `age.empty() or deceased.empty()`.

constraints.human: Can have age[x] or deceased[x], but not both

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, any instance with both `age[x]` and any `deceased[x]` choice fails the base resource invariant.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break. Family histories often record that a relative is deceased and may also record age information, so real-world prevalence could be meaningful. Validators will reject records even if each individual element value is otherwise valid.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly dropping age or death information can affect familial risk assessment and clinical interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid inconsistent representation of a relative's current age and death information; use `deceased[x]` to represent age/date at death when the relative is deceased.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a warning/best-practice invariant or a narrower hard rule that targets clearly conflicting age-at-death representations instead of forbidding every `age[x]` plus `deceased[x]` combination.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 invariant has a coherent modeling goal: `age[x]` is the relative's age when the history is recorded, while `deceased[x]` can carry death status or age/date at death. Making the rule a base error is disruptive, but the alternatives leave material ambiguity and safety risk when both fields are present.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have started with a warning invariant, profile-level constraint, or a narrower rule that allows `deceasedBoolean` with `age[x]` while prohibiting combinations that encode competing age facts. That would preserve common R4 records, but it would not fully achieve the R6 base goal of forcing one unambiguous representation for deceased relatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves more old records but weakens the base guarantee against ambiguous live-age versus death-age data.

evidence.detail: R4 contains fhs-1 and fhs-2, but no fhs-3 age/deceased invariant.
R6 adds an error invariant `age.empty() or deceased.empty()`.
evidence.quote: Can have age[x] or deceased[x], but not both

note.text: R4 ageAge=68 was present; review whether it represented age at death or age when history was recorded.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example intentionally does not pretend a lossless automated transform is always possible; the meaning of the old `age[x]` must be assessed.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a local error invariant that makes `age[x]` and `deceased[x]` mutually exclusive. This is a hard break for R4 data that used `age[x]` plus `deceasedBoolean`, `deceasedDate`, or `deceasedAge` to describe a deceased family member.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with both fields can be valid under R4 local constraints but invalid in R6. This affects validators, import pipelines, and generated model validation. It is not a major R6-to-R4 problem because R4 is less restrictive.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Before R6 validation, detect instances with both fields. If `deceased[x]` already carries age/date at death, preserve `deceased[x]` and remove or annotate `age[x]`. If `age[x]` is the only age information and `deceasedBoolean=true`, manual policy is needed: it might be age at death, age when history was recorded, or approximate current-age data entered inconsistently. Include regression cases for all `deceased[x]` choice types.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been staged as a warning or profile constraint to avoid base validation failures. The hard R6 invariant is more consistent but requires explicit migration decisions for historical records.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This is the most likely local hard validation break for clinically meaningful existing data.

findings.title: `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` were merged into `reason: CodeableReference`

oldState.summary: R4 had separate repeating `reasonCode` CodeableConcept and `reasonReference` Reference elements.

binding.description: Codes indicating why the family member history was done.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 separated coded/textual reasons from references to resources justifying the family-history event.

newState.summary: R6 has a single repeating `reason` element of type CodeableReference, preserving the same reference target list and example binding for concept content.

binding.description: Codes indicating why the family member history was done.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 element combines concept and reference representations through the R6 `CodeableReference` datatype.

facts.oldValue: CodeableConcept plus Reference on separate elements

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 definition text combines the R4 reasonCode and reasonReference definitions and keeps the same binding and target profile list.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using either old element name are invalid in R6 until transformed. Runtime/codegen risk is high because two generated properties become one property using an R6 datatype not present in R4. R6-to-R4 conversion can be lossy when one `CodeableReference` item carries both concept and reference, because R4 has separate arrays without an item-level association.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The reason for collecting family history can affect interpretation and workflow, especially when tied to a specific diagnostic report, observation, questionnaire response, or condition.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt the R6 `CodeableReference` pattern for fields that can be either a concept or a resource reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` alongside the new `reason: CodeableReference` during a transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Standardizing on `CodeableReference` is a reasonable R6 goal and can represent an associated concept/reference in one repeated item, which the old parallel arrays did not model cleanly. A compatibility transition was possible, but the duplicate-field tradeoff is substantial enough that the breaking merge is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would keep the two R4 fields, mark them deprecated, and add `reason` for new CodeableReference-style content with guidance or invariants to avoid conflicting use. This covers existing R4 instances but only partially meets the R6 unification goal, because systems would need to support two representations of the same reason indefinitely and decide how to synchronize or prioritize them.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces immediate wire/API breakage but creates duplicate same-resource representations and synchronization ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `reasonCode` as 0..* CodeableConcept with example binding to clinical-findings.
R4 defines `reasonReference` as 0..* Reference to Condition, Observation, AllergyIntolerance, QuestionnaireResponse, DiagnosticReport, or DocumentReference.
R6 defines `reason` as 0..* CodeableReference with the same target profile list and clinical-findings example binding.
R6 CodeableReference has optional `concept` and optional `reference` children.

examples.examplesMd: The R6-to-R4 example is problematic because a single CodeableReference item can associate a concept and a reference; splitting into R4 arrays loses that association.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 replaces two R4 reason elements with a single `reason` element using `CodeableReference`. This is a high-impact migration pattern because it changes JSON property names, generated APIs, and conversion logic even though the underlying concept/reference target semantics are mostly preserved.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 content under `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` is old-valid/new-invalid until transformed to `reason[].concept` or `reason[].reference`. Valid R6 content is not always cleanly representable in R4 because R4 has no `CodeableReference` datatype and no way to preserve a concept/reference pair as a single repeated item.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 `reasonCode` entry to one R6 `reason.concept` and each R4 `reasonReference` entry to one R6 `reason.reference`. For R6-to-R4, split simple concept-only and reference-only entries back to the corresponding arrays, but flag entries containing both children or extensions for manual review or extension-based preservation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is understandable as a standardization on `CodeableReference`, but a compatibility transition with deprecated old fields would have avoided immediate validation failures. The tradeoff would be duplicate fields and potential synchronization rules.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Check downstream serializers and FHIRPath expressions for both old field names; this change is easy to miss because the business label "reason" stayed the same.

findings.title: R6 adds a family-history `procedure` backbone not representable in R4

oldState.summary: R4 had no local procedure backbone on FamilyMemberHistory.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 FamilyMemberHistory could record conditions and notes, but not a structured list of procedures performed on the related person.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional repeating `procedure` with mandatory `procedure.code` when present and optional outcome, contributedToDeath, performed[x], and note.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can now directly capture significant procedures in a family member's history.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional element does not invalidate R4 data moving to R6, but it creates a substantial R6-to-R4 gap. Structured family procedure history cannot be represented in the R4 base resource without extensions, notes, or a separate modeling convention.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Family history of procedures can be clinically significant, for example prophylactic surgery or transplant-related family history.

justification.inferredGoal: Expand FamilyMemberHistory beyond conditions to include significant procedures for relatives.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not an R4-to-R6 breaking base-design issue: optional R6 `procedure` content preserves all R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding an optional procedure backbone expands the R6 resource for a plausible clinical use case and does not invalidate R4 instances. The compatibility concern is mainly that R6 procedure history cannot be represented natively in R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this is additive optional R6 content, no less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility. Not adding the element, or using only an extension, would reduce R6-to-R4 down-conversion pressure but would also fail the apparent R6 goal of making family-history procedures discoverable and standardized in the base resource.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 round-trip loss; extension or profile approaches are down-conversion mitigations, not backwards-compatible base R6 alternatives.

evidence.detail: No R4 `FamilyMemberHistory.procedure` element exists.
R6 adds `procedure` as 0..* BackboneElement.
R6 requires `procedure.code` 1..1 when a procedure backbone is present.

examples.examplesMd: The procedure can be placed in an R4 extension or note, but there is no native R4 FamilyMemberHistory element with equivalent structure.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a structured `procedure` section for procedures the related person had. This is useful new expressiveness, but it is a round-trip breaking change for R6 systems that must emit R4 because the base R4 resource has no procedure backbone.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken because the new element is optional. R6-to-R4 representability is high risk: an R6 instance containing `procedure` must either use an extension, degrade to narrative/note, or lose structured procedure details.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 interfaces, define a standard extension or profile rule for `procedure` before data exchange. If only a narrative note is possible, mark the conversion as lossy. Test procedure entries with `performedAge`, `performedDateTime`, outcomes, and contributed-to-death flags.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding an optional base element is backward compatible for R4-to-R6 but not for down-conversion. A cross-version extension would be more compatible but less visible and less likely to be implemented consistently.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Do not map procedures into `condition` unless a local clinical governance rule explicitly accepts that semantic loss.

findings.title: R6 adds `recorder` and `asserter` actors

oldState.summary: R4 had no local `recorder` or `asserter` elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could represent author/source details only through other resources such as Provenance, extensions, or surrounding workflow context.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional 0..1 references for who recorded and who asserted the family member history.
newState.narrativeMd: `recorder` captures who recorded the history; `asserter` captures who is making the statement. `asserter` additionally permits Device.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The additions are optional and do not invalidate R4 data. They do create a down-conversion gap because R4 FamilyMemberHistory has no native fields for the same actor roles, and using Provenance is not a field-level equivalent.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Actor provenance can matter for trust and audit, but it is usually less clinically direct than condition/procedure content.

justification.inferredGoal: Capture source/recording accountability directly on FamilyMemberHistory.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not an R4-to-R6 breaking base-design issue: optional `recorder` and `asserter` additions preserve all R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Direct recorder and asserter fields support a reasonable accountability/source goal and are optional, so they do not create old-valid/new-invalid instances. The remaining compatibility issue is how to down-convert or ignore new R6 actor details in R4 systems.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The backward-compatible-alternative label is not applicable because the base R6 additions do not break R4 instances. A Provenance-only or extension-only approach could have helped cross-version round-tripping, but it would trade away the usability and uniformity of direct base elements rather than preserve an otherwise broken R4-to-R6 path.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is R6-to-R4 actor-provenance loss; Provenance or extensions are mitigations rather than less-breaking base alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `recorder` 0..1 Reference with seven target profiles.
R6 adds `asserter` 0..1 Reference with eight target profiles including Device.
R4 has no same-named local elements.

examples.examplesMd: An R4 export can carry this information in Provenance or extensions, but not in the base FamilyMemberHistory element set.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds provenance-like actor fields directly to FamilyMemberHistory. These additions are not R4-to-R6 breaking, but they are important for systems that must round-trip or down-convert R6 data to R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data remains valid when converted to R6. R6 data using `recorder` or `asserter` is not cleanly representable in the R4 base resource and will be lost unless an extension or Provenance mapping is defined.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 exchange, decide whether to create R4 Provenance resources, use cross-version extensions, or omit the actor data with a lossy-conversion flag. Test all allowed target resource types, especially `Device` on `asserter` because it has no matching `recorder` target in R6.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are generally backward-compatible upward, but cross-version compatibility would have been better served by standard extensions or Provenance guidance. Direct elements trade down-conversion simplicity for R6 usability.

findings.title: `condition.code` semantics widened to include allergy or intolerance

oldState.summary: R4 described `condition.code` as the actual condition suffered by the relation.

binding.description: Identification of the Condition or diagnosis.

semanticText.definition: The actual condition specified. Could be a coded condition (like MI or Diabetes) or a less specific string like 'cancer' depending on how much is known about the condition and the capabilities of the creating system.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 text frames the backbone as conditions or diagnoses.

newState.summary: R6 describes the same element as condition, allergy, or intolerance suffered by the relation.

binding.description: Identification of the Condition or diagnosis.

semanticText.short: Condition, allergy, or intolerance suffered by relation
semanticText.definition: The actual condition, allergy, or intolerance specified. Could be a coded condition (like MI or Diabetes) or a less specific string like 'cancer' depending on how much is known about the condition and the capabilities of the creating system.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 broadens the allowed meaning without changing the element path, type, cardinality, or example binding.

facts.newValue: Condition, allergy, or intolerance suffered by relation
The actual condition, allergy, or intolerance specified...

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a syntax validation break, but it is a semantic compatibility risk. R6 data may intentionally encode allergies or intolerances under a path that R4 consumers understand as a condition/diagnosis, potentially changing business rules or clinical interpretation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Confusing allergy/intolerance family history with condition history can affect clinical decision support and displays.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow FamilyMemberHistory to represent allergy or intolerance history for relatives without adding a separate backbone.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not an R4-to-R6 instance-breaking issue: the path, type, cardinality, and binding are unchanged, so existing R4 instances remain structurally valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of representing family allergy or intolerance history is plausible, but the local evidence does not explain why that meaning was widened under a path named `condition`. The change preserves wire compatibility for old data yet can mislead R4-era consumers that attach condition-specific business rules to this element.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Since no R4 instance becomes invalid, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable under the calibration rubric. A clearer R6 design could add a distinct allergy/intolerance backbone or classifier, but that is a semantic clarity tradeoff rather than an alternative needed to preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A separate allergy/intolerance model would reduce semantic ambiguity but adds model surface; it is a clearer R6 design alternative, not a backwards-compatible rescue for invalid R4 instances.

evidence.detail: R4 definition refers to the actual condition specified.
R6 definition refers to the actual condition, allergy, or intolerance specified.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is syntactically shaped like R4, but its R6-intended meaning as allergy/intolerance is not what the R4 element text described.

findings.narrativeMd: The same `condition.code` path now explicitly covers allergy or intolerance. A strict schema may accept the same JSON shape in both versions, but the intended meaning has broadened, which can break business logic that treats all `condition` entries as diagnoses or conditions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid merely because of this text change. The risk is still-valid-but-behaviorally-different and R6-valid/not-cleanly-R4-semantic: an R6 allergy/intolerance entry can be parsed by R4 code but interpreted under older condition-only assumptions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 conversion, identify entries that are allergies or intolerances and decide whether to preserve them with an extension, narrative note, or local profile. Update displays and decision support so they do not assume every condition backbone entry is a diagnosis.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broadening could have been less ambiguous with a distinct element or explicit classifier. Reusing `condition` minimizes structural change but pushes semantic discrimination to terminology and local business rules.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding depends on semantic text, not cardinality/type. Human clinical review may be needed to decide whether allergy/intolerance content belongs in R4 exports.

findings.title: `condition` and `condition.code` became summary elements

oldState.narrativeMd: Family-history condition details were not part of the R4 summary projection according to these element flags.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 summary representations may include condition entries and their codes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Summary flag changes do not make instances invalid, but they can change `_summary=true`, generated summary DTOs, sparse payloads, indexing assumptions, and privacy/data-minimization expectations.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Condition summaries are clinically useful but may reveal more information in summary responses than some R4-era clients expected.

justification.inferredGoal: Make the core family-history condition content available in summary views.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not an R4-to-R6 instance-breaking issue: changing `isSummary` affects summary behavior, not base instance validity.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Making the core family-history condition and code available in summaries is a reasonable R6 goal because they are central to the resource. The change can affect sparse payloads and privacy expectations, but it does not make old instances invalid.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The alternative-availability label is not applicable because the finding is runtime behavior only. R6 could have left the flags unchanged and relied on `_elements`, profiles, or server policy for summary inclusion, but that would reduce default summary usefulness rather than preserve structurally broken R4 content.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Leaving flags unchanged would avoid runtime surprise but make default summaries less clinically useful; this is a summary-behavior tradeoff rather than an instance-preserving base alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 `condition` isSummary is false.
R6 `condition` isSummary is true.

examples.examplesMd: No instance fragment is needed: the same instance can be valid in both versions while summary serialization behavior changes.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 marks `condition` and `condition.code` as summary elements. This can change what servers return in summary mode and what generated summary models contain, even though ordinary validation is unaffected.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not old-valid/new-invalid. It is a runtime/API compatibility issue: summary views may include condition content in R6 where R4 clients did not expect it, and privacy filters based on summary flags may need reassessment.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review `_summary`, `_elements`, generated lightweight models, caching, and redaction rules. Add tests comparing summary responses for FamilyMemberHistory with conditions so client contracts are explicit.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is reasonable if condition code is considered essential summary data. A backward-compatible alternative would keep summary flags unchanged and let implementations opt in, at the cost of less informative default summaries.
